newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European bourses close higher, dollar strong.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European bourses close higher, dollar strong.

text.p: European bourses ended well up on Friday as bargain-hunters snapped up stock unloaded because of jitters over Wall Street's poor performance this week.

On currency markets, the dollar ended the European session stronger, setting a 33-month high against the ailing yen and steady against the mark as hopes grew that German interest rate cuts were still possible.
European bourses, their confidence sapped by a poor performance in New York on Thursday, slipped at the start as investors took profits from the recent bull run.

But London and Paris bounced back and ended up over 0.5 percent. In Frankfurt, computerised transactions also ended the day strongly but floor trading closed in the minus column after clawing back some losses.
The European bourses were given a boost when Wall Street perked up after an unsteady opening caused by inflation worries when U.S. data showed orders for manufactured goods jumped in September.

The Commerce Department said new orders for durable goods rose 4.6 percent, the largest increase in nearly four years, to a seasonally adjusted $174.1 billion as strong demand more than erased a very weak showing in the prior month.
Markets on both sides of the Atlantic climbed as investors digested the figures and apparently concluded they did not hold threats of higher interest rates.

"The overall number suggests goods production is still moderate and does not demand any immediate attention from the Fed (central bank)" said Waldo Best, senior economist at BZW Securities Inc in New York.
In London traders said they expected cash-rich institutions would use recent declines as an opportunity to increase equity holdings.
"You will have nervous bouts from time to time but there are too many people out there sitting with surplus cash," said the head of equity trading at one leading brokerage.

London's FTSE 100 undex had earlier sunk further below the 4,000 mark, extending three days of losses against a background of Wall Street weakness where the Dow fell 44 points on Thursday to below 6,000, a key benchmark breached two weeks ago.

In Paris, stocks reversed their early losses to close up 10.81 points at 2162.43 points. Rhone-Poulenc was a star performer, climbing 3.16 percent after the group announced a big rise in third-quarter net income.

Frankfurt recovered most of its losses as investors interpreted its central bank's hints of lower interest rates as good for business. Floor trading ended marginally down but computerised deals ended well up.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar perked up against the mark after the news on prospects for German interest rates. It slipped slightly towards the end of the session.

Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said a further cut in the German securities repurchase rate would be possible mid-term under certain circumstances. He told reporters while attending a conference that in the medium term "a repo rate cut is still possible depending on developments."
The U.S. currency also hit a peak of 113.35 yen as the belief took hold that Japanese interest rates would remain low for some time.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 1.5210 marks and 113.30 yen in late European trading compared with 1.5230 and 112.90 yen on Thursday.
STOCKS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 23.0 points higher at 4,022.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 10.81 at 2,162.43.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 4.21 at 2,674.22.
PRECIOUS METALS

Platinum ended at $383.40, off $2.50, on New York-led technical selling after briefly dipping below gold for the first time in nearly three years. Gold closed slightly weaker at $382.70 an ounce, down 40 cents. Silver finishes one cent up at $4.92.
